topic: Decoding Wordle: Using Information Theory to Win

sections.title: Introduction: The Guessing Game
sections.content: Introduce Wordle as a decision-making game under uncertainty. Define the goal: minimize the number of guesses by maximizing 'information gain' per turn.
sections.example: A 'Wordle-bot' (a cartoon owl) faces a 5-letter word puzzle. Instead of guessing randomly, it evaluates the 'surprise' value of its choices.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Measuring Uncertainty with Entropy
sections.content: Introduce Shannon Entropy (H). Explain it as the average amount of 'information' produced by a stochastic source. Visualize this as a 'Probability Tree' where branches represent possible word outcomes.
sections.example: Graphical chart: A pie chart showing the distribution of remaining possible words. Entropy is the measure of how 'flat' or 'spiky' this distribution is.

sections.title: The Core Logic: Information Gain
sections.content: Explain that every guess splits the remaining word pool into smaller subsets based on the color-coded feedback (Gray, Yellow, Green). The 'best' guess is the one that splits the pool into the most balanced groups, effectively maximizing the expected information gain.
sections.example: Animation showing a word like 'CRANE' splitting a set of 2,000 words into 50 distinct color-pattern buckets, versus a word like 'XYLYL' which leaves most words in one giant bucket.

sections.title: Application: The Strategy in Action
sections.content: Demonstrate the iterative process: 1. Calculate entropy for all valid words. 2. Pick the word with the highest score. 3. Update the candidate list based on feedback. 4. Repeat.
sections.example: A visual flow diagram where 'CRANE' (the input) filters a dictionary of 12,972 words down to a narrow list of 50, showing the entropy plummeting from high to low.

sections.title: Conclusion: Summary and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize that winning at Wordle isn't about vocabulary; it's about systematically reducing the 'state space' of unknown information. Final takeaway: Entropy is the tool to transform guessing into solving.
sections.example: Final slide: The cartoon owl transforming from a frustrated guesser into a 'Master Architect' who visualizes the game as a narrowing funnel of data.
